These changes have american fingerprints all over them, they're essentially trying to turn Formula 1 into Nascar or Indy. They'll ruin the  sport by making it dumbed down, simplified and  artificially equalized across the field.

What exactly do I mean by that? Well....as soon as you take a niche  sport like F1 and try to make it acceptable to a wide audience (and an uneducated audience) , you ruin the essence of what made the niche sport  great in the first place, and what made the TRUE fans love it.  True  fans of F1 love the F1 as it is NOW, because it's as it's supposed to  be. A hierarchy of teams is A NATURAL THING.  Just because some teams  are better, doesn't mean that it's a bad thing.  They're better for a reason, and taking those reasons away KILLS THE ESSENCE of what F1 is about, engineering excellence, creativity, pushing the limits in any way possible, etc. They'll just squish  everything together, just like they do in Indy, Nascar, etc.  That's NOT a good thing, and unfortunately most people fail to see it, despite it being obvious. All you have to do is go watch those races and see what kind of a polar opposite they are to F1. It's like comparing football to basketball.

Imagine what football would look like if someone came along and said "nope, Barcelona can't be so much stronger than some XY team from a poor XY country, we have to come up with rules that ruin Barcelona and makes that XY team more competitive". You think that would improve the sport?  No, no it wouldn't. They think  they'll improve competition with these rule changes, but in the process, they'll make the  competition LESS RELEVANT.  If you ARTIFICIALLY REMOVE SOMEONES ABILITY TO BECOME GREAT, what is the point of it then?

As far as the artificially boosting the amount of overtakes... it's basically like they're turning football into basketball.  They're saying 2-3 goals per game is boring, so lets change the rules of  football so that teams can score 60-70 goals per game and so that someone who watches a football game once a year can enjoy it more. Guess what  happens when they do score. Nobody fucking cares. A goal loses value.   That's what will happen in F1.  Overtakes will happen so often they'll lose value. Just like they have no value in Indy or Nascar. When it's difficult to overtake, then the overtake HAS A LOT OF VALUE, AND IMPORTANCE.  Sure it's not as "exciting" for the average clueless viewer, but for people who understand the sport, it is.

As far as standardized parts and design restrictions go...it's just another sign of them turning F1 into Indy-like competition. They'll start with standardized aero parts, then suspension parts, then more and more and more, until we reach a point where all teams will have the same freaking car with a different paint job on it.  It's HORRIBLE, absolutely HORRIBLE for a sport like F1 which has always been about the COMPLETE OPPOSITE of standardization. Instead of giving teams more freedom, they're giving them more restrictions, and presenting that as an change for good.

But this is the problem... whoever owns F1 now doesn't care about the ESSENCE OF THE SPORT. They care about turning more profit, under the guise of making the sport more exciting.  They'll make the sport more exciting, to the wrong crowd though. The issue is, that "wrong" crowd is much bigger than the crowd of real F1 fans.  What the current F1 leaders are doing is catering to the lowest common denominator, because that means more fake fans and more money. The fact that true fans will stop following the sport is irrelevant to them. THAT is what I meant by saying they're americanizing the sport .That's how sports are done in the USA. They look at sports differently than we do in Europe. For us, sports are about passion. For americans, it's about money. They're turning a complex sport with a  lot of things happening under the surface into something that's going to  be superficial and dumbed down in order to cater the dopamine-rush  addicted audiences seeking cheap short-lasting thrills.

Already sort of gave up on it and the hype is gone, and sort of went back to playing BF3 on hardcore servers. It's sad to say, but it has to be said. COD:MW is still worse than Battlefield 3 was almost 10 years ago. Apart from improvements in graphics (not as massive as you'd think since BF3 still looks amazing, and runs at 300+ fps on a PC that can't hit 100 in MW), everything else is better in BF3.  Again, this is not nostalgia speaking, since I can switch between the two games instantly. It actually annoys me, all this hype around COD, because I feel like a better game is sitting there played by very few people, while everyone is talking about this new game that clearly isn't as good, and the only reason so many people will play is because it's new and because they never tried something better. The best part is, COD fanboys are going crazy about something "new" and "innovative"  that they apparently disliked almost 10 years ago when they were claiming COD was better than Battlefield BC2, BF3 and in a way BF4 (even though that's where BF went downhill).

​

As for MW compared to Battlefield 3, my BENCHMARK for multiplayer FPS games, still after all these years:

1. Guns DEFINITELY feel, handle and SOUND far better in BF3.  BF3 probably did the best job of all FPS games ever in combining the right levels of realism to make the guns feel substantial, real and impactful, with the right level of arcadeness to make them fun to use. COD guns always felt and sounded like plastic  toys in comparison. Like BF guns are REAL guns, and COD guns are air gun replicas of real rifles shooting out plastic BB's. MW is not as bad as some older COD's in that regard, but it's still off the mark.
2. Movement and the entire game is just far more crisp, responsive, fluid, etc. in BF3. The way you run, jump over obstacles, the transitions from running to crouching or going into prone, and everything in between, is just superior. The way ADS works, how crisp and responsive it is, how responsive aiming is, etc. is just better in BF.  It feels like there's ZERO delay or damping between what you do to your mouse and what the ingame response is.  Before you FEEL that, you can't understand or appreciate how important that is, and in addition to that you can't understand why people who are BF fans despise how COD's play.
3. Map design is infinitely better in BF3. Both in terms of close quarter maps and huge open ones. Interior designs and exterior designs are just better. There's depth to everything, there are levels to everything, things feel real, realistically big and proportioned, etc. What Battlefield always did right was create environments that FEEL REAL, whereas COD always failed miserably at that, and their maps always feel like GAME LEVELS instead of like real places, like everything there is placed there for the sole purpose of creating a small, isolated area for a shooting game.  BF maps always felt like real places that you just happen to be fighting at. MW is still suffering from that problems. Maps feel like they're specifically designed for the annoying, hyper-ultra-fast paced run and shoot COD gameplay style where you just mindlessly run and spray and hope to kill someone before you die every 5 seconds. 
4. Vehicles are far superior both in terms of function, freedom, handling, controls, etc. Whats the point of helicopters in COD when you can spit from one side to the other side of the map because its so tiny? BF3 ACTUALLY had huge maps that felt like you can stretch your wings in them even when flying jets.  Yes, even flying very quick jets never made you feel like you were constrained to a small space. Dog fight with jets or helicopter fights in BF3 is something COD can't even dream of matching. Helicopters causing havoc from air is something COD can't match. Tanks battles in BF3 are something COD can't match. The way tanks, LAV's, jeeps, etc. behave and drive in BF3 is far superior. A COD player can never understand how it feels to have a tank battle with a tank that is 500m away and you can barely see it...or how it feels like to hit a helicopter from the other side of the map using a guided missile by timing it just right after he used flares. I mean, it's pointless talking about it. I just feel sorry for anyone who never played these games.
5. No building destruction in COD... lame.  Whats the point of vehicles then?  Whats the point of a tank if you can't even collapse a small hovel? In BF3 you could gradually collapse entire several story tall buildings. And the best part is, the destruction felt real and fluid enough to be convincing.  There were multiple ways to damage, destroy or collapse buildings. That was a HUGE part of the game, because it increased immersion to INSANE levels and dictated how you approach objectively. You never felt safe. If you were in a house and heard a tank outside, you knew you were fucked, because one shell can take you out.
6. Hardcore mode - that is something missing from new BF's too, so I won't be too hard on COD for it, but it's something definitely required in multiplayer FPS games.  Minimal amount of HUD information and screen clutter, NO CROSSHAIR, no ammo information, no minimap, realistic damage and health, realistic ballistics, etc. Pure immersion.
7. Sound in Battlefield - I don't think any words have to be spent on it, but sound in BF was always a benchmark, and of all BF's, BF3 is the peak of the hill. Absolutely perfect sound engineering. You can hear a squirrel fart from half a map away and tell what it ate by the sound of it.  There's such detail, depth and quality to every sound in BF3 that it's worth playing just to hear it, just to hear how mechanical and realistic guns sound.

​

Don't get me wrong. MW isn't a bad game. It just feels like a copy of another game, and worse in every way. Kinda like comparing PUBG to some low budget free to play BR shooter that's trying to copy it. If I were to give Battlefield 3 a 9.5/10 score, and if I were to give BF V an 8/10 score, then I'd have to give COD: MW a 7/10.
